newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFFER says executive pay a shareholder matter.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFFER says executive pay a shareholder matter.

text.p: Electricity industry regulator (OFFER) Stephen Littlechild said on Monday executive pay was a matter for shareholders and the company, not the regulator.
But the OFFER director general told the House of Commons Public Accounts Committee that regulators should maintain a tough line on overall company costs.

Littlechild said: "I can appreciate that the companies perhaps have not handled this matter in a way that is entirely satisfactory. Having said that, it is not clear to me that it would be sensible for me as a regulator to start dictating to companies how much they should pay their senior executives."
Littlechild said it was hard for the regulator to work out what the going rate for a director was.

But he added: "It seems to me the most appropriate thing is to take a tough line on all their costs, including their executive and manpower costs, and leave it to the company, to the shareholders who monitor the company, to decide how best to take this forward." -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7768
